newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend advance on trade data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend advance on trade data.

text.p: Mexican stocks posted sharp gains on Wednesday to close above the 4,700 point mark for the first time this week as players stepped in to buy in the wake of stronger-than-expected trade data, dealers and analysts said.

"The market had flagged but picked up again and uncoupled itself from the Dow Jones industrial average when the trade data were announced...there were buyers, but I suspect they were day-trippers as volume was pretty thin," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 89.93 points, or 1.93 percent, at 4,742.12.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 76 to 27 out of a total of 122 stocks traded. Volume was more moderate than for many recent sessions at 94.4 million shares.

The Finance Ministry announced in early dealing that Mexico had chalked up a preliminary trade surplus of $182 million in June. This compares with an average of $165 million predicted by 12 local financial firms in a Reuters survey.
Dealers said trade figures underpinned confidence as many of them had very fresh memories of burgeoning deficits that led to a shock devaluation in 1994 and an ensuing financial tailspin.
Analysts said falls in primary rates at Tuesday night's central bank auction had given stocks an early shove that ran out of steam on caution over the crop of second-quarter earnings reports.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates fell by 53 basis points to 18.72 percent on Tuesday night.

"After recent turbulence over Brazil and hard profit-taking the market is now waiting for earnings reports..., some of which will be better than others and we will see that in intraday movements," said independent consultant Carlos Escalante.
Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was the most heavily traded gainer, accounting for over 10 percent of the day's market volume.
The stock rose 22 centavos (3 cents) to 19.88 pesos ($2.54) -- a smaller percentage gain than the overall market -- as investors were lukewarm toward earnings it posted the night before.

One of Mexico's biggest financial groups, Bancomer, recovered from a recent slide to end up 31 centavos (4 cents) at 4.66 pesos (59 cents). Traders said interest rate cuts could ease the group's past-due loans burden.
